## Why This Is Asked
This question probes end-to-end streaming NLP design for multilingual real-time chat with privacy, retrieval-augmented inference, drift handling, and governance.

- On-device inference for privacy
- Retrieval-augmented NLP over a live KB

- Governance for high-risk outputs and rollbacks
- Low-latency streaming architecture

## Code Example

```python
# Simple drift metric between two distributions
import math
def kl_divergence(p, q):
    return sum(pi * math.log(pi/qi) for pi, qi in zip(p, q) if pi > 0 and qi > 0)
```

## Why This Is Asked

Ensures evaluation captures real-world drift, multilingual and code-switching complexities, and privacy constraints on edge deployments.

## Key Concepts

- Multilingual, code-switching evaluation
- Drift detection (embedding KL, population stability index)
- Privacy-preserving data handling (synthetic data, DP budgets)
- Canary rollouts and rollback criteria
- Edge latency and memory constraints

## Code Example

```python
def evaluate(model, dataset):
    preds = model.predict(dataset)
    f1 = macro_f1(dataset.labels, preds)
    per_lang = {lang: f1_lang(dataset[lang], preds)}
    drift = kl_divergence(model.embeddings, dataset.reference_embeddings)
    return {"f1": f1, "per_lang": per_lang, "drift": drift}
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you adapt to sudden entity distribution shift (new slang, new names)?
- How would you validate privacy-preserving labeling without ground truth?

```python
# Lightweight on-device classifier skeleton
from typing import List

def extract_bow_features(text: str, vocab: List[str]) -> List[int]:
    tokens = text.lower().split()
    return [1 if w in tokens else 0 for w in vocab]

def predict(text: str, vocab: List[str], weights: List[float], bias: float) -> float:
    x = extract_bow_features(text, vocab)
    score = bias + sum(w * xi for w, xi in zip(weights, x))
    return 1.0 if score > 0.5 else 0.0
```
